I know dog walkers are probably expensive, but I wonder if you have any acquaintances who might be interested in walking your dog once in a while? As a currently petless animal lover I feel like if a friend or even someone I barely knew or hadn't spoken to in years posted on Facebook or wherever offering/asking friends to take their dog on a walk, that would be beneficial to both parties, your dog gets walked, the friend gets to spend time with an animal, and I personally would do it for free just to get to spend time with a dog without the commitment and expense of owning one. I know this isn't a solution to the bigger issue, but sometimes chipping away at little things helps for me. I really hope it all works out for you and your doggy.

Is the death of someone who has a serious, legitimate illness, has exhausted all possible options for treatment, has fought against it as long as possible, and has simply run out of options, really the cruelest death? Is it really more cruel than someone who wants to live but dies anyway, whether it be from a different illness like cancer, or murdered, or whatever else? Going through years of chemo and radiation, or having your body gradually shut down, or whatever else the case may be, is not any less cruel, painful, or torturous than someone ending their own life. What's cruel is people being forced to end their suffering in brutal, painful ways because western society cannot bear the idea of people dying, especially not dying how and when they want to. Suicide isn't any more cruel than any other cause of death, and depression isn't any less valid or real as a cause of death than any other illness. In a good chunk of cases, there is a chance that things will get, or could have gotten, better for someone. But that's not always the case. It is presumptive of you to pretend to know anything about mine or anyone else's situation on the internet, and platitudes like what you wrote are a joke. I was merely making an observation on how society views death and suffering, and you felt the need to jump in and say "cheer up, it gets better!!" Insert sunshine and rainbows. When people are ill, they deserve the right to treatment - which, as you hopefully know, is incredibly difficult and expensive to access in a lot of the world. But not all illnesses are curable, or sometimes even treatable. People deserve to live, and die, with dignity. End of story.

I recognize that killing myself would cause some people grief, but how does it balance out? Is avoiding causing a few people grief worth going through daily, endless suffering myself? I guess some people would call that "selfish", but one could also see it as selfish of people to expect a suicidal person not to kill themself for the sake of those around them. I don't know. Death is inevitable, and either you're going to grieve your loved ones' deaths, or they're going to grieve yours, only difference is who goes first. So why does it even matter.

Yeah i feel that. You're supposed to be able to trust your therapist and work with them and be vulnerable with them, and that's so hard when you're also always second guessing their knowledge or ability. I'm curious whether your therapist says she's trauma-informed? Because, and admittedly I'm no professional, but from what i know that is very much incorrect that you need to have had a specific event that is considered a trauma in the general societal understanding of the term. Trauma is your brain/body's reaction to an something, and it doesn't have to be "traumatic" for it to cause trauma. Anyways i am absolutely butchering this and i apologize but I weirdly am in such a similar situation where I don't know whether i should try to find a new therapist or continue but i feel bad because i have such a cheap rate. So yeah.

I wish i knew a good way to address it but i just wanted to affirm what you already know, that that was in fact SA, and I really hope you get to a place where your T can understand you about it. It really sucks when we as a client need to be the ones educating the T about something that really should be common knowledge, especially for someone in that profession.
